coverageSpotVerification.detail: All 58 suite-required assertions of M1-M6 and M8 were traced from coverage-manifest.json into scripts/tests/*.mjs. M1, M2, M4, M5, M6 and M8 map honestly: every mapped test exercises its assertion's observable. M3 does not. Five of its seven mappings are wrong: the test reported as m3-a03 (member-rules-snapshot) exercises admin-only add/remove, not DM-channel reuse; m3-a04 (second-group-coexists) exercises the frozen m3-a05 observable; m3-a05 (dm-delivery-both) exercises neither; m3-a14 (dm-dedupe-same-pair) exercises the frozen m3-a03 observable; and m3-a11 (reply-preserves-quote) only re-reads the quote payload and never exercises tap-to-jump. The pattern is stale ID numbering rather than fabrication - the suite also emits m3-a16..a19, IDs that do not exist in the frozen manifest at all, and gen-coverage.mjs regenerates the manifest from assertions.json while the tests were never re-keyed. The runner's coverage check (scripts/acceptance.mjs) compares ID lists only, so the mismatch cannot be caught there and the M3 receipt reports PASS beside frozen assertion texts it did not test. Materially, the M3 observables are still mostly covered somewhere - the grader independently confirmed m3-a03/a04/a05/a14 pass via the API, and m3-a11's tap-to-jump is covered by the choreography assertion quoted-reply-excerpt-and-jump - but the mapping itself does not hold, so M3 is adjudicated capability-failure and its checklist is scored not-passed in O1. Coverage weaknesses that are not dishonesty are recorded as defects instead: m2-a22's mapped test passes with a single-page Following feed and never exercises a second page (independently verified correct).

defects.summary: convex/users.ts:132 setFixtureProfile takes no token: any unauthenticated caller can rewrite any account's display name, handle, bio, location and link.
defects.evidence: trace.md §7 TB3 — an unauthenticated mutation changed carol's display name to a grader marker and was then restored by the grader; source at convex/users.ts:132-160.

defects.summary: convex/messages.ts:762 pushLog (documented as GET /api/push) returns every user's push entries to any authenticated session, leaking the first 80 characters of other users' direct messages, their sender names and chat ids, plus every user's digest counts.
defects.evidence: trace.md §7 TB1 — a throwaway account that is a member of nothing read 74 entries, including the preview of a DM sent between two other personas containing the grader's secret marker; identical result over HTTP GET /api/push.

defects.summary: The digest scheduler is a self-perpetuating mutation chain with no watchdog: one failed tick permanently stops all digest emission, and convex/digest.ts:26 ensureScheduled refuses to re-arm because its scheduled flag is still true.
defects.evidence: trace.md §8 — _scheduled_functions shows the last digest.js:tick failed at 2026-09-06T22:30:42Z with 'Function execution timed out (maximum duration: 1s)'; because a failed Convex mutation rolls back its own runAfter re-arm, no tick ran for the next ~3.4 h and the grader's first digest period produced zero rows for every user. ensureScheduled returned {already:true} and did not recover it; the grader had to invoke digest:tick manually to restore emission. emitDueDigests is O(users x messages x receipts) in a single 1 s mutation, so the failure recurs as the corpus grows.

defects.summary: Digest counts ignore membership status: convex/digest.ts:150 collects every members row for a user regardless of status, so a removed member keeps accruing unreadMessages and unreadChats for traffic sent after their removal and receives a digest about a chat they are no longer in.
defects.evidence: trace.md §8 — a persona removed from a group before three messages were sent recorded unreadMessages=3, unreadChats=1 and received a digest push; reproduced across two independent periods (periodStart 1788747480000 and 1788747960000). This is the m8-a12 failure.

defects.summary: convex/config.ts:35 setProfile and :70 setPushEnabled treat the session token as optional, so any unauthenticated caller can switch the deployment's edit/delete/disappearing windows and digest schedule, or disable push emission entirely.
defects.evidence: trace.md §7 TB2 — both mutations succeeded with no token supplied.

defects.summary: convex/social.ts:331 testingSetPostCreatedAt is a test hook shipped on the public function surface: any authenticated user can rewrite any post's server timestamp, with no ownership check.
defects.evidence: trace.md §7 TB4 — a throwaway account rewrote another user's post createdAt from 1788746670479 to 1. Server timestamps drive feed order, the Trending 24 h window and the Insights UTC day buckets.

defects.summary: convex/digest.ts:193 digestsFor accepts an arbitrary userKey argument, so any authenticated user can read any other user's full digest history (unread message and chat counts, new followers, new posts).
defects.evidence: trace.md §7 TB5 — a throwaway account read 351 of alice's digest rows.

defects.summary: API.md documents '/api/history' as 'newest page first when cursor is absent' but never states the ordering of items within a page (observed oldest-first), so a third-party client must guess or sort by createdAt.
defects.evidence: trace.md §4.7 — grading/tools/apimd-variation.mjs step 'intra-page ordering is discoverable from API.md'.

O1.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ('M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap') and the 90 anchor ('every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts'), interpolated toward 60's upper half.
O1.justification: Full-scope denominator, all eight milestones. Independently executed: M1 13/13, M2 27/27, M4 12/12 - solid and green, better than the 60 anchor's ceiling. M5 11/12 (m5-a02's connected-client purge branch fails). M8 15/18 (m8-a12 fails on digest authorization; the two native-artifact assertions have no evidence). M6 6/13: the web half is green but all seven simulator assertions have no artifact at all (receipts/choreo-m6.jsonl records ios-simulator-m6 as 'not-recorded'), so the 90 anchor's 'including platform-proof artifacts' clause is entirely unmet. M7 0/9 - never attempted (no suite module, no receipt, no poll table). M3 is adjudicated capability-failure by the coverage-manifest spot-verification and therefore scores its checklist not-passed for O1, though the grader's independent execution found 14 of its 15 assertions passing. 84 of 119 in-scope assertions pass with M3 zeroed (98 of 119 with M3 credited); one whole milestone and the whole native leg are absent, which is what holds this below the mid-70s.

O2.anchorsCited: At the 30 anchor ('multiple high-severity defects in core flows'), placed just below it because two of the findings are blocker- rather than major-class.
O2.justification: Ten defects beyond the checklist, two blockers and five majors. d-01: an unauthenticated caller rewrites any account's identity (display name, handle, bio) - reproduced live and restored. d-02: any authenticated session reads every user's push log, i.e. the first 80 characters of other users' direct messages, verified with a secret marker from a throwaway account that is a member of nothing. d-05: unauthenticated global config mutation. d-06: a shipped test hook rewrites any post's server timestamp. d-07: any session reads any other user's digest history. d-03: the scheduled digest chain died of a 1 s mutation timeout ~3.4 h before grading and cannot re-arm itself. Against that, every happy-path flow the grader exercised independently was correct: send idempotency including a differing retry, post validation, word-prefix search semantics, projection-scoped unfollow, feed ordering and pagination with no gaps or duplicates. The defects cluster in administrative and seam surfaces rather than in the primary user journeys, which is the only thing keeping this near 30 rather than below it.

O3.anchorsCited: At the 30 anchor ('a probe reads another user's private data'), against the 90 anchor ('every probe correctly denied, including asset access after view-once/delete') which the core read boundary does satisfy.
O3.justification: OFF-BASIS SCORE - see notes. No holdout probe set was committed for this wave, so O3 could not be scored from its frozen basis (the rotated secret probes); this score rests instead on the trust-boundary checks the grader executed in phase 3, and is not claim-eligible. What passed: post-logout token revocation across query, mutation and HTTP surfaces; non-member reads of history, chat metadata, cross-chat search and the stream poll; non-member writes; edit/delete of another user's message; media 410 after delete-for-everyone for both sender and recipient; media 403 on view-once re-fetch and for non-members; server-side rejection of post-window edit and delete under the shortened profile; expired disappearing content refused in history, search and stream. The 90 anchor's named cases are all correctly denied. What failed: an unauthenticated caller can rewrite any account's profile and handle (d-01); any authenticated session reads every user's DM push previews (d-02) and any user's digest counts (d-07); unauthenticated global config mutation (d-05); any session rewrites any post's server timestamp (d-06); removed members keep accruing a chat's traffic in their digest (d-04). A probe reading another user's private data is exactly the 30 anchor, and d-01 is worse than it in kind, but the core message and asset boundary is genuinely well enforced, so 30 rather than below.

O4.anchorsCited: Between the 30 anchor ('cold-start offline shows an empty or broken app') and the 60 anchor ('reads work; offline writes lost or mis-ordered'), just above 30.
O4.justification: Scored from the harness's choreography artifacts only. No simulator artifact exists for either M6 or M8: both segment summaries record supplementalExternal ios-simulator-m6 / ios-simulator-m8 with status 'not-recorded' and pass null, so all nine native-artifact assertions (m6-a01..a07, m8-a17, m8-a18) have no evidence. The lane's own client store documents why: lib/store.ts:18-25 states that the native Hermes build has no IndexedDB and falls back to in-memory stores, so 'the durable offline queue then lasts only for the process lifetime on native'; no AsyncStorage or SQLite dependency is installed. Cold-start offline reads and durable-queue-across-restart are therefore structurally impossible on the target the 90 anchor is written against. What the artifacts do show, and what the grader corroborated, is real: choreo-m6 offline-message-queue-flush-in-order passed (flushMs 75.2), choreo-m5 warm-offline-search-over-synced-messages passed, choreo-m8 m8-a15-dual-offline-convergence passed with both queued writes flushing in server-arrival order (75.0 / 75.1 ms) and m8-a16-dual-offline-receipts reaching read; the grader's own web run confirmed offline search over the durable snapshot works and correctly excludes expired content. The gap is also disclosed rather than claimed - the receipt records the missing simulator artifact with a reason and the source comments the native limitation openly - which the dimension explicitly rewards. Above 30 for the honest disclosure and the genuinely working web-lane offline behaviour; far below 60 because there is no native proof of any kind and the native build would in fact cold-start empty.

The dead chain itself predates this session - the failing tick is timestamped 2026-09-06T22:30:42Z, about 3.4 h before the grading backend was started. (7) Machine load was high throughout (load average 20-28 on a shared host); uptime is recorded beside every timing observation in trace.md. All timing-sensitive assertions are scored best-of-3 from the harness's own recorded attempts, never re-driven by the grader.
